newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends down on funds, hedges and CBOT.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends down on funds, hedges and CBOT.

text.p: WCE canola and flaxseed futures ended lower on fund and hedge selling, as well as on a sharp downturn in CBOT soy complex futures, traders said.
"We followed Chicago. Funds liquidated a couple of hundred," a trader said.

"There was scattered selling on the snow in Alberta, people are worried about taking delivery of this stuff. Fear's keeping us from pounding canola," another said. Jan-Mar spread at $0.50, Nov-Jan at $3, Nov-May $1.90.
November canola fell $3.60 to $433.80 per tonne, January lost $4.70 to $436.50. Volume was 5,375 lots with 450 hedges.
October flax fell $0.50 to $398, November down $2 to $375. Oct-Nov spread $23 as shorts rolled into November. Volume 161.
October feed wheat rose $0.90 to $197.90 on local short covering, Dec fell $1.30 to $181.50. Oct-Dec spread at $15.50. Volume was 1,300 lots. Oats did not trade.
"Feed wheat's got another C$20 (a tonne) to go down to be in line with the world, it's C$30 over barley," a trader said.
November western barley rose $0.90 to $148 on feedlot buying, February rose $0.10 to $152.10. Nov-Feb spread at $4.50. Volume was 2,000 lots.
Cargill bought one job lot of December feed peas from UGG, down US$2.20 at US$207, traders said.
(All values in Canadian dollars except peas, oats)
